title: The Ominous Chamaeleon I Dark Cloud
caption: The Chamaeleon I dark cloud, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA. Image Processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image captures the ominous Chamaeleon I dark cloud, described as the nearest star-forming region to Earth. Within it sit three reflection nebulae, lit up brightly by stars that have only recently formed nearby.

Chamaeleon I is one part of the larger Chamaeleon Complex. Dark clouds like this are dense concentrations of cold gas and dust, thick enough to block the light of stars behind them, and it is inside such clouds that new stars take shape. A reflection nebula works differently from the glowing gas of an emission nebula. Its dust simply scatters the light of nearby stars toward us, much as fog brightens around a streetlamp.

The image was captured with the 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera, fabricated by the Department of Energy, on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope. That telescope stands at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, which is a Program of NSF NOIRLab.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g and i filters and a narrow N662 filter. The color mapping isn't published.
